[LTIM.2.6.2] A time-dependent condition on a rule with more than one positive
pattern is a compile error `DS_VALIDATE_NOW_MULTIPATTERN_UNSUPPORTED` rather than a
silently non-re-evaluating rule. Both kinds count: a `where` that makes any
time-dependent read, a clock, a series or a zone read ([LTIM.2.4.1]), and a
positive pattern's `within` window ([LTIM.2.7.1]). A `then …
within` step does not: its window compares two facts' `ts` values ([RLOW.5.6.1]) and
reads no clock. A cache read is not time-dependent, and [LEXP.9.6.1] refuses it
under its own code.

The compiler counts `t.local(tz)` and `t.date(tz)` ([LTIM.10.3]) as a zone read
unless `tz` folds to `"UTC"` ([LTIM.10.8]): a literal, or a `const` whose folded
value it is ([LGRA.4.1]). A designation it cannot fold may name any zone when the
rule runs, so it counts, whatever it holds.
